Her Himācala-daughter birth caused forgotten knowledge; she must recover it and see heart Gaṇeśa as Mahāmāyā.

Śiva lists eight Gaṇarāja avatāras and Brahman correspondences: Vakratunda tvam; Ekadanta tat; Mahodara asi; Gajānana Sāṃkhya; Lambodara Brahman in Śakti; Vikaṭa sat/Sun; Vighnarāja sama/Viṣṇu; Dhūmravarṇa unmanifest neti/Śambhu. They are kalā forms governing eight Brahmans, supported by self-experienced Brahman; ayoga has no play, Svānanda does; full yoga transcends both. Śiva calls Gaṇeśa family deity, daily worships Cintāmaṇi/Vināyaka as light of five mental activities and shows jeweled elephant-faced household image and secluded meditation place to astonished Pārvatī.

Pārvatī asks how universal deluding Śakti became wife of partial/tamasic Śiva. He recounts seeing her power in five-deity rivalry; after Gaṇeśa instruction he propitiated her100 years. She appeared, invited boon, accepted hymn and request to be his wife, granted and vanished. Her left limb emitted Lakṣmī beloved of Nārāyaṇa, right Sāvitrī beloved of Brahmā, heart Saṃjñā wife of Sun. Śiva urges recovered Gaṇeśa yoga; Pārvatī privately practices, gains peace quickly through former impressions and returns to him. Mudgala tells Dakṣa wholehearted Gaṇeśa worship will remove obstacles/grief and make him honored yoga lord.
